newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Patrick Child briefed on the 1997 annual economic report adopted by the Commission on Wednesday. Child said the report was not a pre-selection of participating countries for Economic and Monetary Union but a starting point for the economic orientations to be adopted at the June European Council. He said Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy would present the report to the European Parliament on February 25 at 1700/1600 GMT.
In answer to a question, Child said the deficit and debt figures for 1996 mentioned in the report were not definitive. He said definitive figures would be obtained by March 1.
In answer to a question, spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the EU-Israel trade deficit would be solved by bringing the two economies closer and intensification of trade relations.

Vale de Almeida said Commission President Jacques Santer would meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Tuesday only if the European Parliament's agenda allowed him to be in Brussels that day.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/109: EU calls for final push on WTO telecoms talks.
- Speech/97/39: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson on the fifth research framework programme.
- Eurostat news release No 13/97: EU unemployment falls to 10.8 percent in December.
- Eurostat news release No 14/97: Member states invest 51.5 billikon Ecus in EU partners.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and finance No 1997-1: Gross domestic product, official figures for 1995.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and finance No 1997-2: EU 15 current account transactions with its main partners: the USA and Japan.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and finance No 1997-3: EU direct investment inflows.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and finance No 1997-4: Comparison in real terms of the gross domestic product for the EU, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Poland - 1995.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Distributive trade, services and transport No 1996-10/11/12.
